content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson focuses on introduction to algorithm analysis within Mathematical Foundations and Complexity Analysis. Start with the specific syllabus items rather than memorizing names: What Is Algorithm Complexity?; Time Complexity and Space Complexity; Input Size and Basic Operations; Analyzing Statements and Loops. Identify the input, the supported operations, and the condition that makes the algorithm correct.

content_blocks.title: How the subtopics connect
content_blocks.text: The PDF lists the following concepts for this lesson: What Is Algorithm Complexity?; Time Complexity and Space Complexity; Input Size and Basic Operations; Analyzing Statements and Loops. Treat these as connected parts of one problem-solving workflow. Define the state and assumptions, perform the operation, preserve the needed invariant, then inspect the output.

content_blocks.title: Correctness checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Breadth-first search (BFS) explores a graph in layers; with equal edge costs it finds shortest paths by edge count. Before relying on the result, state your preconditions, identify the invariant or key argument, and test an input that violates a common assumption.

common_mistakes.why: A normal case may hide empty-input, duplicate-value, ordering, disconnected-input or off-by-one errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, boundary and invalid cases and state which inputs the implementation supports.

common_mistakes.problem: Guessing complexity from the code length.
common_mistakes.why: Loops, nested work, recursion, data structure operations and input properties determine the cost.
common_mistakes.fix: Count dominant operations as a function of input size and distinguish auxiliary memory from input storage.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a code snippet as a complete production implementation.
common_mistakes.why: A teaching example often omits input validation, robust tests or special cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the linked exercise and local tests to extend it; record runtime assumptions and limitations.
